summary: The two additions address distinct declared subconditions and the content actually returned by lookup. No new actionable P0-P2 was found within the four-file proposal. Existing reported-number, declared aggregation and shared-original rules remain intact. This verdict establishes neither application nor measured repair effectiveness.

hunks.purpose: Distinguish declared observations by subject, state and delivery path within one item; distinguish preparatory or review conclusions from the observations supporting them.

Use returned content and range as read coverage; distinguish file metadata and original-log coordinates from current excerpt offsets; do not turn an empty EOF or an unread page into a substantive result.

delta_identity.template_interfaces: Proof/lookup section names, variables, verdict tool contract and all baseline lines remain unchanged.

adjudication.basis: The addition is conditional on the metric requiring different subject/state/delivery-path observations. It prevents one observed condition or a preparation summary from being substituted for another required observation. It does not require all metrics to include such distinctions, invent a new condition, or prescribe a path/actor list.
adjudication.relevance_to_reported_counterexample: It is a suitable generic instruction for separating judge-input observations and external-acceptance observations from other observations in the same item. The actual159 replay omissions and their severity are a separate semantic audit; this review did not read that cohort.

adjudication.axis: Actual returned content versus locator metadata
adjudication.basis: File name, total byte size and source-coordinate metadata do not establish that the response contained the required observation. The new paragraph explicitly follows returned content/ranges, permits another targeted read or an honestly unverified condition, and does not infer failure or absence from empty EOF.
adjudication.locator_scope: Original full-log coordinates may differ from offsets in an extracted local file. The proposal distinguishes them without rewriting any locator, retained input or canonical criterion.
adjudication.interface_limit: The instruction refers to returned offset/next_offset values; it does not create a tool field or permission. This four-file review does not independently validate every lookup adapter schema or observed pagination response.

adjudication.basis: Candidate lines42-43 retain the explicit prohibition on undeclared reruns or extra proof for metrics measuring a reported number. The new separation of summaries and underlying observations does not turn a declared reported-number metric into an execution metric. No source/raw-read requirement is added to every metric.

The unchanged lookup ending permits aggregation of multiple executions according to the declared method while preserving their identifiers/scopes. The additions introduce no one-run-only rule, numeric gate, fixed call count or ban on combining declared observations. Whole-CI failure and individual successful checks can still coexist.

Candidate line46 explicitly permits one original that actually contains observations for several conditions; unchanged reason instructions also permit explaining such conditions together. Distinguishing observations does not require separate files or tool calls for each condition. A single returned body containing both relevant observations remains usable for both.

The proposal requires the necessary observations, not every byte or every page. A partial reply can suffice if it contains those observations. If it does not, the prompt permits further targeted lookup or keeping the condition unverified. Existing REJECT rules apply only where the declared target cannot be established; EOF itself is not made a negative observation.

No host gate, timeout, budget, schema, lookup permission, lifecycle transition, extra approval actor or Goal requirement is introduced. Read-only lookup, the separation of verifier judgment from human confirmation, and rejection of role-changing instructions remain as before. Existing verdict/reason requirements are retained rather than newly expanded by this patch.

proposal_plan_assessment.narrow_design: Fresh finite partial-content negative/positive controls with recorded observations after a page boundary, plus a reported-number control, are relevant to the proposed instructions. They are a prospective design, not existing execution evidence.
proposal_plan_assessment.locator_followup: Separately identifying original versus excerpt coordinates is compatible with preserving the76 retained inputs. That proposed followup has not been implemented or evaluated by this reviewer.
proposal_plan_assessment.independent_axes_limit: The stated partial-content controls would primarily exercise content-range reasoning. Success there alone would not establish correct actor/state/delivery-path distinctions in arbitrary metrics or close the specific A3/A7 omissions.
proposal_plan_assessment.no_reliability_claim: Any later finite-control verdicts need their actual inputs, tool results and stored outcomes. This review predicts neither model compliance nor a success rate.
